chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the sacrificial animal (hady) if it became defective before reaching the place of slaughter, does it suffice for its owner? He said: 'If it is a voluntary sacrifice, he should slaughter it and eat from it, and it has sufficed for him whether it reached the place of slaughter or not; there is no compensation due on him. And if it was a guaranteed (borrowed/due) sacrifice, he is not required to eat from it whether it reached the place of slaughter or not, and he must provide its equivalent.'

key_terms.اَلْهَدْيِ: Sacrificial animal offered during Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a sacrificial animal becomes defective before slaughter?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of hady defects by distinguishing between voluntary (tatawwu') and guaranteed (daman) sacrifices, ruling that voluntary defects incur no fidya while guaranteed ones require replacement. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that the validity of voluntary worship is not contingent upon the animal's physical perfection at the time of slaughter, whereas guaranteed obligations demand full restitution. The narration highlights the practical application of 'daman' (liability) in ritual sacrifices, ensuring that the spiritual intent is preserved even if the physical vessel is imperfect.
